title: Touring New England with a tab show
summary: While in Boston Waters worked in Bobby Hargrave's tab show around Maine and Vermont, with street ballyhoo, and the show landed two weeks at the Lafayette Theater in New York.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: OK, Benny, I wanted to ask a question. Remember when we were talking about Philadelphia, where it came up that occasionally you went out of town with both Charlie Miller and Lonnie Polk. While you were in Boston you got some out-of-town work, too, which included your first trip to New York.

Yes, well that, now that, that's something altogether different. See, I, the time that I stayed in, up there in Boston, I also did some little things in the New England states like Bangor, Maine and Vermont and up in that way, see. So this - and I worked with a tab show also - and the band was, a little guy, one of them guys in the band was named Bobby Hargrave, a little violin player, you know, see, a little, he from New York, around here. Anyway -
H-A-R-G-R-A-V-E (BW joins PS for the last 5 letters), Hargrave, right?
V-E, Hargrave, yeah. See, so we joined a little, what did we call it, tab show, you know what a tab show means?
No, no, a tab show is somethin' like down at the Village Gate -
Uh huh - oh, you mean like 'One Mo' Time?'

Yeah. We call that a tab show, I mean you know, see, it's a old things, old songs, old jokes, you know. That's what we call a tab show, I don't know how it exactly got its name. Anyway, I joined this little tab show in the period that I wasn't working, you know what I mean, when you're stayin' in places you're not workin' all the time, see. See, so I joined this band and we did tours not so much in Boston because it wasn't good enough for Boston. But we'd go up in the country, you know, see, in Maine, Vermont, you know, those little hick, we call Hickville. That's what tab means, playin' in those little hick towns, you know, see. They used to ride round the street before the show in a wagon, all that kind of stuff, blowing in a wagon - sometimes a truck and sometimes had a horses too, you know. And just before the show, you know, ballyhoo with 'em 'Yeah, the show goes on, the so-and-so'. So I stayed with that show, then the show got to be not too bad, you know, it worked out not too bad. So it got a job in the Lafayette Theater (laughs), see, you know? They got a couple of weeks in Lafayette Theater, it wasn't too good, though. But we did come to - and we got paid. So we - in
